fresh.verdict:
The handover is a good overview, and it is enough to rebuild the same preview on the laptop and to find a frame on disk. It is not enough to do the other five tasks safely. Every laptop and repo path it names exists, and the Oracle paths check out (img 274 recursive, clips 48, stillclips 10, send_preview_tg.sh present). There are four places where following it as written goes wrong:
(1) The re-take command overwrites the existing, md5-locked clip. Its model is elided, and its budget variables are undocumented cumulative caps.
(2) The compile always mixes in the voice and music she has put on hold. It cannot build a cut without voice or text, and the shot list sits in an unmentioned array in build_cut.py that also drives the glitches and the cover shot.
(3) There are three numbering systems, and "frame 14" is ambiguous between them.
(4) Oracle's disk is 100% full (219 MB free), and Oracle's own film9.mjs is the pre-fix version that froze the server. Neither fact is in the handover.
The $0 still-motion option and the stanza-change path have no runnable recipe. The money figure cannot be refreshed from the document. The laptop copy of the handover does not exist yet, and the handover, cut.json and frames_map.txt are all untracked.

issues.detail: Running the documented re-take command `node gen.mjs video v<shot> venice` OVERWRITES the clip already in the cut and in the md5 manifest. gen.mjs writes to `clips/<shotId>__<tag>.mp4` with renameSync and has no exists-guard. So re-taking v15 destroys Oracle's only `v15__venice-kling-o3-pro.mp4`, which breaks rule 9 and the manifest's 47 locked clips.
issues.evidence: Oracle gen.mjs veniceVideo(): `const dest = path.join(BASE, 'clips', `${shotId}__${tag}.mp4`)` … `fs.renameSync(dest + '.part', dest)`. video() has no existsSync check. FILM9_APPROVED_MANIFEST lists 47 clips with md5s.
issues.fix: Add a 're-take recipe' block. (1) Back up plan.json: `cp plan.json plan.json.bak-pre-<shot>r2-<date>`. (2) Write a docs/atuona/film9_retake_<shot>_<date>.py that copies plan.shots['v15'] to a NEW key such as 'v15r2', with any motion-text change she approved. scp it and run it with python3. (3) Run gen.mjs on 'v15r2', which produces `clips/v15r2__venice-kling-o3-pro.mp4`. State plainly: never re-run gen.mjs video on an existing shot id.

issues.section: §4.2 Motion (re-take command and budget env vars)
issues.detail: The command elides the model (`VENICE_VIDEO_MODEL=…`). Without that variable, gen.mjs falls back to wan-3-0-pro-image-to-video at a different price and writes `v<shot>__venice.mp4`. BUDGET_USD and VENICE_BUDGET_USD are CUMULATIVE ledger caps (total spent so far + this job), not per-run limits, and the document never says this. The real run used VENICE_BUDGET_USD=84.08, which would now refuse every call because Venice ledger spend is $85.83. With BUDGET_USD=110 and no Venice cap, the guard allows $13.91, more than the $12.61 in the wallet.
issues.evidence: gen.mjs line 250: `model = process.env.VENICE_VIDEO_MODEL || 'wan-3-0-pro-image-to-video'`. guard(): `if (s + usd > BUDGET)` with s = sum of all succeeded ledger rows. ~/atuona-film9/run_motion.sh: `export BUDGET_USD=110 VENICE_BUDGET_USD=84.08 …`. Ledger now: total 96.09, venice 85.83, replicate 10.27.
issues.fix: Write the exact command, with numbers and the meaning of each: `cd ~/atuona-film9 && nohup env VENICE_VIDEO_MODEL=kling-o3-pro-image-to-video VENICE_OMIT=aspect_ratio,resolution BUDGET_USD=<96.09 + approved $> VENICE_BUDGET_USD=<85.83 + approved $> node gen.mjs video v15r2 venice > logs_motion/v15r2.log 2>&1 &`. It polls for up to 20 minutes. Add: 'caps are cumulative: run `node gen.mjs ledger` first and add only the amount Elena approved'. Also name run_motion.sh and motion_run_ids.txt as the batch form.

issues.section: §4.6 Compile / §7 Open decisions (tighter cut, voice and music on hold)
issues.detail: The document says music and voice are on hold, but any rebuild following §4.6 puts BOTH back in. The compile has no switch to leave them out: it throws when a shot with a stanza has no vo/<sid>.mp3, it always mixes CUT.music, and a shot with its stanza removed gets the literal word 'undefined' burned on screen. So 'voice: none' or 'key stanzas only' ($7.3) cannot be built without a code change. The agent is not told this, and is not told what the next preview should contain by default.
issues.evidence: atuona-film9.mjs l.139-140: `if (noVo.length && !--stanza-preview) throw new Error('missing voice: …')`. l.177: `fs.writeFileSync(txt, spread(it.stanza))`, where spread(undefined) returns 'undefined'. l.39/262: MUSIC is always an input. build_cut.py hardcodes `'music': 'music/film9_deephouse.mp3'` and asserts every slot has a stanza.
issues.fix: Add to §0/§7: 'Until Elena decides, a rebuild still carries all 39 voice lines and the deep-house track she called ugly. Say so in the Telegram caption, or ask first. A cut with no voice, partial voice, no music or no text needs a small change to scripts/atuona-film9.mjs (e.g. FILM9_NO_VO=1 skips the voice check and the voice mix; FILM9_NO_MUSIC=1 uses anullsrc; text drawn only when it.stanza is set). That is a repo code change: Teach → Plan → Confirm with her.'

issues.section: §4.6 Compile (make a tighter cut from shots she names)
issues.detail:
The document never says where the shot list lives. It is the hardcoded ORDER array in build_cut.py. Several traps are also undocumented:
- The 3 approved glitches are tied to shots 7, 11 and 14 (GLITCH_AFTER), so dropping one of those shots silently drops its glitch.
- `cover: '1a'` makes the compile crash (`cover.it` of undefined) if 1a is cut.
- The script uses relative paths, so it must run from the repo root.
- It writes over cut.json, the untracked file the preview was built from.
- Its date line '08.10.2026' is hardcoded.
- `--reuse` reuses pv_seg_<sid>.mp4 by shot id only, so any shot whose clip, trim or stanza changed must be listed in `--reseg=`, or the old segment goes in silently.
issues.evidence: build_cut.py: `ORDER = ['1a','1b','1c','2',…]`, `GLITCH_AFTER = {'7': 'G7.jpg', '11': 'G8_clean.jpg', '14': 'G6s.jpg'}`, `'cover': '1a'`, `json.dump(cut, open(f'{W}/cut.json','w'…))`. atuona-film9.mjs l.176 reuse test is by `seg_${it.sid}` only. `git status`: `?? docs/atuona/film9_stanza_work/cut.json`. A dry run confirmed the current cut.json is exactly what build_cut.py produces.
issues.fix:
Add a 'tighter cut' recipe:
- cd to the repo root.
- Copy build_cut.py to build_cut_tight.py, or add an ORDER/OUT env var. Set ORDER to her shots in film order, and write `cut_tight_<date>.json`.
- Keep GLITCH_AFTER on surviving shots (or ask her where G6s/G7/G8 go), and set cover to a kept shot.
- Pass `FILM9_CUT=…/cut_tight_<date>.json`.
- Use `--reuse --reseg=<every changed sid>`.
- Commit cut.json now as the record of the 8 Oct preview.

issues.detail:
Three numbering systems collide, and the document names none of the mappings:
- Position in frames_in_film_order (01–39, no card): '14' = shot 13 = img/k13.
- Section number in FILM9_STANZAS.md (1–40, card 1c is #3): '14' = shot M2.
- Shot id (1a…37, M1…M5): shot 14 is position 15.
On top of that:
- '7m' vs '7' is never explained.
- Image names differ from shot ids (16b = k16m, 25 = k25m, 35 = k36).
- If she says 'the shot at 2:10', the time-to-shot map is render_local/work/timeline.json, which the document never mentions.
- frames_map.txt, the position→image map, is untracked.
issues.evidence: frames_map.txt: `14_13 k13`, `15_14 k14`, `20_16b k16m`, `37_35 k36`, `06_7m k07m`, `07_7 k07b`. The FILM9_STANZAS md has 40 sections starting '## 1. Shot 1a', '## 2. Shot 1b', with section 3 = card 1c. render_local/work/timeline.json has 39 rows {shot, clip, poem, start, dur}.
issues.fix: Embed one 39-row table in the handover: position NN | shot id | official image (img/kNN.jpg plus its same_bytes_as alias) | clip used | poem # | start time in the 5:24 preview (from timeline.json). Add the rule: 'when Elena gives a bare number, it is the NN prefix in 02_APPROVED/frames_in_film_order. If in doubt, ask her and send that thumbnail back.' Commit frames_map.txt.

issues.detail:
Still-motion is offered as the $0 alternative, but there is no command for it. In fact:
- It runs on Oracle as `~/atuona-film7/venv/bin/python still_motion.py render sm/specs/<name>.json`, via run_sm.sh with nice -n 12 and -P 2.
- The depth model is ~/atuona-film7/models/depth_anything_v2_small.onnx.
- Oracle's system python3 has no cv2, and the laptop has cv2 but no onnxruntime.
- Depth maps (sm/depth/*.png) and specs exist only on Oracle.
- Specs hardcode base_dir ~/atuona-film9 and out `stillclips/sm_<name>.mp4`, so re-rendering overwrites the clip in the cut.
- It is a video render on Oracle, which conflicts with the 'NEVER render video on Oracle' rule.
issues.evidence: run_sm.sh: `ls sm/specs/*.json | xargs -P 2 … ~/atuona-film7/venv/bin/python still_motion.py render {}`. film9_still_motion_fallbacks_2026-10-08.py: `'base_dir': os.path.expanduser('~/atuona-film9') … 'out': f'stillclips/sm_{name}.mp4'`. Oracle `python3 -c 'import cv2'` gives ModuleNotFoundError. Laptop: `import onnxruntime` gives ModuleNotFoundError, while cv2 5.0.0 is present.
issues.fix: Add a still-motion recipe and decide where it runs. Laptop option: scp the depth PNG and spec, set base_dir to the laptop APPROVED folder and out to a NEW name (sm_<name>_v2.mp4), then `python scripts/atuona-still-motion.py render <spec>`. Oracle option: only with her OK, one at a time, under nice, after a memory and disk check, using the film7 venv path above. Note that new frames need a depth map, which needs onnxruntime and the model.

issues.detail: The change path is not described. The text flows picks.json → verify_picks.py → translation → stanzas_final.json → build_cut.py → cut.json, and verify_picks.py only checks picks.json, not stanzas_final.json. The voice script skips any shot whose vo/<sid>.mp3 already exists, so the old voice would read the old text over the new stanza. The burned-in segment is reused unless that sid is in --reseg. The readable FILM9_STANZAS .md/.html exists only in the laptop folder, with no generator, so it goes stale.
issues.evidence: verify_picks.py: `picks = json.load(open(f'{W}/picks.json'))`. atuona-film9-vo.py: `if not (os.path.exists(out) and os.path.getsize(out) > 2000):` (skip). `git grep FILM9_STANZAS_2026-10-08` hits only the handover; the file sits in D:\ATUONA_FILM9_ALL_MATERIAL_2026-10-08\01_STANZAS\.
issues.fix:
Add a stanza-change recipe:
- Edit slot <sid> in picks.json and stanzas_final.json (back them up first). English = her text verbatim from poems_github_2026-10-08.json. Russian = atmospheric English that keeps every image and adds nothing.
- Run `python docs/atuona/film9_stanza_work/verify_picks.py` from the repo root.
- Rebuild cut.json.
- If voice is used, move render_local/vo/<sid>.mp3 into vo/_replaced/ before re-voicing (paid, needs her go).
- Rebuild with `--reuse --reseg=<sid>`.
- Update the stanza .md/.html by hand, or commit them to the repo so a generator can follow.

The command also leaves out the static-ffmpeg PATH: the script calls ffprobe after each PAID TTS call, so it crashes after the first purchase. It never says the call costs money and needs her go.

issues.detail: The encode step gives only partial flags: no input, codec, output name, or bitrate rule for other lengths. The scp destination and working directory are not given. The file name collides with the 44 MB phone file already sitting in ~/atuona-film9. The Telegram token and chat id exist only in Oracle's .env (not the laptop's), so Oracle is the only send route, which interacts with the full disk.
issues.evidence: The laptop's cto-aipa .env has no TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, CONCIERGE_TG_CHAT or VENICE_API_KEY lines. send_preview_tg.sh reads /home/ubuntu/cto-aipa/.env and posts `video=@"$1"` relative to its cwd. No phone-encode command is logged in render_local/*.log.
issues.fix:
Give the full commands:
1. `"$FB/ffmpeg.exe" -y -i $R/work/preview.mp4 -vf scale=1280:720 -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -b:v 1000k -maxrate 1400k -bufsize 2800k -c:a aac -b:a 96k -movflags +faststart $R/work/ATUONA_film9_<label>_<date>_phone.mp4`
2. For runs longer than about 5:30: video kbps ≈ 48×8192/seconds − 96. Telegram's hard limit is 50 MB.
3. `df -h /` on Oracle.
4. `scp <file> oracle-cto-aipa:~/atuona-film9/`
5. `ssh oracle-cto-aipa 'cd ~/atuona-film9 && ./send_preview_tg.sh <file> "<caption>"'`; expect 'ok'.
6. Remove the uploaded copy afterwards (you created it this session).

issues.detail:
Several facts needed for a clean run are not written down:
- The command must be run in Git Bash from the repo root, because `node scripts/atuona-film9.mjs` is a relative path.
- A PREVIEW build takes at least 5 minutes (cards at 16:28, preview at 16:33 local), longer than the Bash tool's 2-minute default, so it must run in the background. The 1080p master with minterpolate takes much longer.
- Each run overwrites work/preview.mp4 and the work files in place. The watched preview survives only as the copy in 05_FILM_PREVIEW.
issues.evidence: render_local/work mtimes: card_intro.mp4 16:28, preview.mp4 16:33. preview_build3.log ends 'DONE …preview.mp4 (420.6MB, 323.7s, 39 shots, 39 voice lines)'. atuona-film9.mjs: `final = path.join(W, PREVIEW ? 'preview.mp4' : 'final.mp4')`.
issues.fix: Prefix the block with `cd /d/aideazz/ai-cofounders/cto-aipa`. Add 'run in background; tail render_local/preview_build*.log', and 'for a new cut, use a new FILM9_WORK (e.g. render_local_tight_<date>, with the fonts copied) or copy preview.mp4 aside first'.

issues.detail: Two smaller problems. The document writes the Oracle IP (`ubuntu@170.9.242.90`) into a file headed for the PUBLIC AIPA_AITCF repo, against CLAUDE.md §3 (no hostnames or IPs on public pages); the alias is enough. §6's advice to resume a failed run with `resumeFromRunId` (finished agents replay from cache) applies only inside the Claude Code session that ran the workflow. A new or Cursor session cannot resume those runs, and only translate_workflow.js is saved in the repo.

issues.fix: Use 'ssh alias oracle-cto-aipa' only. In §6, say that the run ids are a record only and that a new session must re-run from the saved script. Save the curation and QC workflow scripts to docs/atuona/film9_stanza_work/ if they are to be reused.

facts.verdict:
Mostly accurate. These claims match their sources:
- the ALL-material folder (916 files, 4.8 GB, the folder counts, README and MD5SUMS);
- the Oracle folder counts (274 images, 48 clips, 10 still-motion clips, 2 music files);
- the ledger totals (Venice $85.82, Replicate $10.27, the 36-clip run at $44.66 with 0 failures, the per-model prices);
- the stanza facts (39/39 verified, 32 poems, 17 RU / 22 EN, the card 1c line from #053);
- every constant and flag in the compile script, the cut.json special shots, the frame aliases, the glitch inserts, the workflow IDs and the memory files;
- the OOM kill itself (ffmpeg, 9.2 GB anon-RSS, no swap, uptime 148 d), and all five health ports plus all five systemd services checking out.

Several points still need fixing before a blind agent can safely continue:
- **Oracle's own `film9.mjs` is the old one-pass build that froze the server**, and the repo script's header still says "Run on Oracle". The handover does not warn about either.
- **Oracle's disk is 100% full.**
- **`openclaw-gateway.service` does exist** (as a `--user` unit).
- **The md5 manifest is stale:** 2 still-motion md5s are wrong and the 4 clips added after it are missing.
- **The budget caps are cumulative totals, not per-run amounts.**
- **`gen.mjs`, the current `plan.json` and the ledger exist only on Oracle.**
- **The claimed handover copies and `cut.json` are not on `main` or on D: yet.**
- **The compile cannot run with "no voice"** without a code change.
- **The freeze lasted about 46 minutes, not 55.**

issues.detail: Oracle's ~/atuona-film9/film9.mjs (20:48 UTC) is the OLD one-pass compile that froze the server. It has no CHUNK batching, no free-memory check and no FILM9_BASE. On top of that, the repo script's own header (scripts/atuona-film9.mjs lines 9-12) still says 'Run on Oracle: cd /home/ubuntu/atuona-film9 && node film9.mjs', and BASE defaults to /home/ubuntu/atuona-film9. Nothing in the handover tells the next agent that running this file on Oracle repeats the 8 Oct freeze.
issues.evidence: ssh: `grep -c CHUNK ~/atuona-film9/film9.mjs` = 0; md5 d6a4e3cd… on Oracle vs fe16c430… for the LF-normalised repo file. The batching was added in commit 3217b76, after the freeze.
issues.fix: Add to §0 and §8: "Oracle's ~/atuona-film9/film9.mjs is the OLD unbatched compile that froze the box. Never run it. issues.detail: 'Always pass BUDGET_USD=<cap>' reads like a per-run amount. In gen.mjs the guard compares the CUMULATIVE ledger spend: BUDGET_USD covers all wallets (now $96.09) and VENICE_BUDGET_USD covers Venice only (now $85.82). Without the env var, BUDGET_USD defaults to 30, so every call is refused. The §4.2 example 'BUDGET_USD=110' with no VENICE_BUDGET_USD would allow about $13.91 more, which is above the $12.61 actually left on Venice.
issues.evidence: gen.mjs line 24: `BUDGET = Number(process.env.BUDGET_USD || 30)`; guard(): `if (spent() + usd > BUDGET) … Refused` and `spentIn(wallet) + usd > VENICE_BUDGET_USD`. run_motion.sh used `BUDGET_USD=110 VENICE_BUDGET_USD=84.08`.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The caps are cumulative ledger totals, not per-run amounts. To allow at most $X more on Venice: VENICE_BUDGET_USD=<85.82+X> BUDGET_USD=<96.09+X> (check `node gen.mjs ledger` first). Without the env vars the default cap of 30 refuses everything."

issues.detail:
Three practical gaps around voice:
(a) The compile refuses to build if any shot with a stanza lacks vo/<sid>.mp3 ('missing voice: … (run vo9.py)'), so 'voice: key stanzas only / none' cannot be built without a code or cut change.
(b) The VO script skips any existing mp3 over 2000 bytes, so a changed stanza keeps its old voice unless a new FILM9_VO folder is used.
(c) The laptop VO command lacks the static-ffmpeg PATH, and the script calls ffprobe, which is not on the laptop's PATH.
issues.evidence: scripts/atuona-film9.mjs line 140: `if (noVo.length && !process.argv.includes('--stanza-preview')) throw new Error('missing voice: …')`. atuona-film9-vo.py: `if not (os.path.exists(out) and os.path.getsize(out) > 2000)` and `subprocess.run(['ffprobe', …])`. On the laptop, `which ffprobe` → not found.
issues.fix: Add to §4.4: "Run with PATH=\"$FB:$PATH\" (the script calls ffprobe). It skips any mp3 already in FILM9_VO, so use a fresh FILM9_VO folder after a stanza changes; never delete the old take." Add to §4.6 / §7.3: "The compile requires a voice file for every stanza shot (line 140). 'Fewer or no voices' needs a small code change to allow a missing vo, after Elena's go."
